source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with trigeminal neuralgia asks for a snack. Which is the BEST choice?
questions.rationale: Light touch or temperature extremes can trigger trigeminal pain, so soft, lukewarm, nutritious foods are best.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q57 (PDF p. 198)
questions.quote: Extremes of temperature will cause trigeminal pain.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement by a client with trigeminal neuralgia shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll avoid cold drafts on my face.'
questions.rationale: Trigeminal neuralgia causes sudden, intense facial pain that is rarely relieved by analgesics. Chewing on the unaffected side and warm mouthwash are recommended.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q764 (PDF p. 993)
questions.quote: The pain is rarely relieved by analgesics.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: In a client with a brainstem injury, which assessment is MOST critical along with the GCS?
questions.rationale: The respiratory center is in the brainstem, so respiratory status and cranial nerve function are critical to assess.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q62 (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: Assessing the respiratory status and cranial nerve function is a critical component of the assessment process in a client with a brainstem injury

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a supratentorial craniotomy, how is the client usually positioned?
questions.rationale: After supratentorial surgery the head is raised about 30 degrees to promote venous outflow and control intracranial pressure.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q111 (PDF p. 260)
questions.quote: the client’s head is usually elevated 30 degrees to promote venous outflow through the jugular veins and modulate intracranial pressure (ICP).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is typical of Guillain-Barré syndrome?
questions.rationale: Guillain-Barré syndrome is an acute autoimmune disorder with ascending symmetrical weakness leading to flaccid paralysis without atrophy, decreased reflexes, and possible respiratory compromise.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q310 (PDF p. 474)
questions.quote: Motor manifestations include ascending symmetrical muscle weakness that leads to flaccid paralysis without muscle atrophy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which measure prevents footdrop in a client with a spinal cord injury?
questions.rationale: Posterior splints or high-top sneakers prevent footdrop (plantar flexion). Heel protectors protect skin, and pneumatic boots prevent DVT.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q333 (PDF p. 499)
questions.quote: The effective means of preventing footdrop (plantar flexion) is the use of posterior splints or high-top sneakers.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After transsphenoidal surgery, what should the nurse tell the client to report?
questions.rationale: Frequent swallowing or postnasal drip may indicate a cerebrospinal fluid leak. Coughing is avoided because it raises ICP.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q338 (PDF p. 506)
questions.quote: The client should report frequent swallowing or postnasal drip or nasal drainage after transsphenoidal surgery because it could indicate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A standing client starts a tonic-clonic seizure. What should the nurse do?
options: Guide him gently to the floor
questions.rationale: The nurse protects the client from injury by guiding him to the floor, turning him to the side, keeping the airway open, and loosening tight clothing. Restraints and tongue blades are never used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q391 (PDF p. 561)
questions.quote: Precautions are taken to prevent a client from sustaining injury during a seizure.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with subarachnoid hemorrhage is on aneurysm precautions. Which intervention promotes safety?
questions.rationale: Aneurysm precautions reduce stimuli that raise ICP. Straining at stool raises ICP, so stool softeners are given and enemas avoided.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q428 (PDF p. 605)
questions.quote: Straining at stool is contraindicated because it increases intracranial pressure.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY in discharge teaching for a client with a spinal cord injury?
questions.rationale: Involving significant others is a priority. The client will need their support, and understanding what to expect helps both cope with the limitations.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q563 (PDF p. 765)
questions.quote: Involving the client’s significant others in discharge teaching is a priority in planning for the client with a spinal cord injury.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement by a client with Bell's palsy shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I wear an eye patch at night.'
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy affects cranial nerve VII. A liquid diet is not needed; the client chews on the unaffected side. Eye protection and facial massage are appropriate.
explanations: Correct answer: a liquid diet is not needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q763 (PDF p. 992)
questions.quote: It is not necessary for a client diagnosed with Bell’s palsy to stay on a liquid diet.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with left-sided Bell's palsy says, 'I don't know how I'll live with this stroke.' What does this show?
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy is inflammation of cranial nerve VII, not a stroke. Many clients wrongly fear a stroke and believe the paralysis is permanent.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q966 (PDF p. 1214)
questions.quote: Although it results in facial paralysis, it is not the same as a stroke.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Kuya Arnel, 28, sustained a C5 spinal cord injury in a construction fall. He is now in rehabilitation.
questions.stem: Which outcome shows his care plan is effective?
questions.rationale: A C5 injury causes quadriplegia with no sensation below the clavicle. Maintaining intact skin is a realistic outcome; the others are not.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q770 (PDF p. 1000)
questions.quote: Maintaining intact skin is an outcome for spinal cord injury clients.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Kuya Arnel, 28, sustained a C5 spinal cord injury in a construction fall. He is now in rehabilitation.
questions.stem: While being bathed, Kuya Arnel says, 'I can't do this. I wish I were dead.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Clarifying by restating invites the client to say more. 'Why' puts him on the defensive, and the others change the subject or give false reassurance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q828 (PDF p. 1064)
questions.quote: Clarifying is a therapeutic technique that involves restating what was said to obtain additional information.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Kuya Arnel, 28, sustained a C5 spinal cord injury in a construction fall. He is now in rehabilitation.
questions.stem: Kuya Arnel says, 'It's so depressing; I'll never have sex again.' What is the REALISTIC reply?
questions.rationale: A sexual relationship is still possible after spinal cord injury, though different from before. Sexual counseling can help with adaptation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q888 (PDF p. 1130)
questions.quote: It is possible to have a sexual relationship after a spinal cord injury, but it is different from what the client will have experienced before the injury.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a thoracic cord injury has an unnoticed red area on the coccyx. After teaching a turning schedule, how should he check his skin?
options: Ask a relative to check daily
Use a mirror to inspect it
questions.rationale: A mirror allows independent skin self-assessment. The client cannot feel the redness, and relying on family does not promote independence.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q772 (PDF p. 1002)
questions.quote: The most effective means of skin self-assessment for this client is with the use of a mirror.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a spinal cord injury has bladder spasms and reflex incontinence. Which instruction helps prevent the problem?
options: Limit fluids to 1 L a day
questions.rationale: Caffeine contributes to bladder spasms and reflex incontinence and is eliminated from the diet. Fluid restriction does not prevent spasms.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q784 (PDF p. 1014)
questions.quote: Caffeine in the diet can contribute to bladder spasms and reflex incontinence

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement by a woman with a T11 cord transection shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Women with spinal cord injury remain fertile, so contraception is needed if sexually active (oral contraceptives may raise thrombophlebitis risk). Limiting dairy helps prevent urinary calculi.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q794 (PDF p. 1024)
questions.quote: Female spinal cord trauma clients remain fertile during their reproductive years

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement by a client with chronic immobility from spinal cord injury needs IMMEDIATE follow-up?
options: 'I don't want to live like this.'
questions.rationale: Expressions of hopelessness or despair need immediate attention because they may mean the client is thinking of self-harm.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q834 (PDF p. 1070)
questions.quote: Expressions of hopelessness or despair require immediate attention

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which assessment BEST tests frontal lobe function in a client with dementia?
questions.rationale: Insight, judgment, and planning are frontal lobe functions. Emotions involve the limbic system, and consciousness the reticular activating system.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q848 (PDF p. 1085)
questions.quote: Insight, judgment, and planning are part of the function of the frontal lobe.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A relative feels guilty for not urging a client with a brain tumor to see a doctor sooner. What should the nurse include in the response?
options: Early signs are easy to spot
questions.rationale: Brain tumor symptoms vary by location (headache, vomiting, visual or personality changes) and are easily attributed to other causes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q889 (PDF p. 1131)
questions.quote: Signs and symptoms of a brain tumor vary depending on location, and they may easily be attributed to another cause.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client recovering from a head injury becomes agitated. Which action BEST calms him?
options: Give him a new task to learn
Turn on music on the TV
Tell him the behavior is bad
questions.rationale: Familiar topics and objects reduce anxiety, and fewer environmental stimuli reduce agitation. New tasks frustrate and TV adds stimuli.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q897 (PDF p. 1140)
questions.quote: Providing familiar objects will decrease anxiety.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client recovering from stroke is irritable and angry about his limitations. Which approach BEST restores motivation?
options: Do tasks for him to avoid frustration
questions.rationale: Supporting and praising accomplishments motivates stroke clients. Behavior is pointed out for correction rather than ignored.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q898 (PDF p. 1141)
questions.quote: It is also important to support and praise the client for accomplishments.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A woman with myasthenia gravis fears her husband will no longer find her attractive. Which action should the nurse encourage?
options: Share her feelings with her husband
questions.rationale: Encouraging her to share her feelings directly with her husband addresses her specific concern. The other responses block communication or avoid the issue.
explanations: Does not address her individual concern.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q938 (PDF p. 1182)
questions.quote: Talking to the client about sharing her feelings with her husband directly addresses the subject of the question.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a complete T1 cord injury says, 'I'm no good to anyone. I might as well be dead.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'I'll ask the psychologist to see you.'
'You feel you're no good to anyone?'
questions.rationale: Restating and reflecting keep communication open and invite him to explore his feelings of loss and unworthiness. Grief is a common response.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q976 (PDF p. 1225)
questions.quote: Restating and reflecting keep the lines of communication open

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Soon after a complete T4 transection, a client insists he will walk once spinal shock resolves. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Denial is a normal early response
questions.rationale: In the first weeks after injury, denial is a normal defense that temporarily lowers anxiety. Prolonged denial can impair rehabilitation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q978 (PDF p. 1227)
questions.quote: Denial may decrease anxiety temporarily, and it is a normal part of grieving.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How can the nurse help the family of an unconscious head-injured client cope?
options: Tell them to grieve outside the room
Limit their questions to the doctor
questions.rationale: The nurse explains equipment, treatments, and procedures and reinforces the provider's information. Displaying grief is normal and should not be discouraged.
explanations: Correct: reduces fear of the unknown.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1018 (PDF p. 1291)
questions.quote: The nurse should explain all equipment, treatments, and procedures

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which family statement shows effective teaching for a client with Parkinson's disease?
options: 'We'll plan only a few daily activities.'
'We'll let him nap whenever he wants.'
'We'll encourage him to take part in his care.'
questions.rationale: Clients with Parkinson's disease tend to become withdrawn and depressed. Active participation in self-care and activities spread through the day prevent this.
explanations: Activities are spread throughout the day.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1022 (PDF p. 1295)
questions.quote: encouraging the client to be an active participant in his or her own care.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which warning signs most likely occurred before a client's thrombotic stroke?
questions.rationale: Cerebral thrombosis develops over hours or days, often preceded by transient aphasia, hemiplegia, or one-sided paresthesias.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1099 (PDF p. 1383)
questions.quote: During the few hours or days before a thrombotic stroke, the client may experience a transient loss of speech (aphasia), hemiplegia, or paresthesias

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a thrombotic stroke, a client has sudden bouts of laughing or crying. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: An expected effect of the stroke
questions.rationale: Emotional lability (sudden laughing, crying, or irritability) is a normal part of the clinical picture after a thrombotic stroke.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1123 (PDF p. 1407)
questions.quote: After a thrombotic stroke, the client often experiences periods of emotional lability

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with myasthenia gravis has vomiting, cramps, diarrhea, hypotension, and facial twitching. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: Cholinergic crisis from overmedication with anticholinesterases causes GI upset, facial twitching, miosis, and hypotension. Medications are withheld.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1135 (PDF p. 1421)
questions.quote: It is caused by overmedication with cholinergic (anticholinesterase) medications, and it is treated by withholding medications.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client develops diabetes insipidus after cranial surgery. Which therapy does the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Diabetes insipidus causes large volumes of very dilute urine. Treatment replaces the fluid losses and gives ADH replacement.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1156 (PDF p. 1443)
questions.quote: The client with diabetes insipidus excretes large amounts of extremely dilute urine.
